claims.claim: bash ./scripts/run_performance_benchmarks.sh completed with exit code 0 on public master commit 7d6ad2f865560cdcca4e30390430a7878c65fa69. The Python harness measured 19 compilation benchmark cases with mean times from 0.0401563915 s to 0.6799075492 s. The highest mean was function_performance.aero, whose median was 0.0417738980 s and whose max run was 6.4224741870 s.
The same public master run completed Rust Criterion lexer-only benchmarks. The reported median tokenization times ranged from 282.31 ns for tokenize_simple_io to 21.507 us for tokenize_large_program.

The GGUF harness completed a real local llama.cpp CLI ROCm inference run with HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 on the Radeon RX 7900 XTX using /home/rob/models/mistralai_Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503-Q4_K_M.gguf. One measured run reported 44.94 eval tokens/s, 186.94 prompt eval tokens/s, and 2701.84 ms load time. This is a llama.cpp CLI backend reference only, not an Aero-vs-llama.cpp-vs-PyTorch comparison.

GPT-2 training versus PyTorch, GPU 4096x4096 Aero matmul speedup, NCCL/MPI multi-GPU scaling, Aero-vs-llama.cpp-vs-PyTorch GGUF comparison, and HIP/vector-add claims are omitted because no current public-branch Aero artifact or rerun verified them.
